Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

2. The instant bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.222 of 2024, under Section 376 I.P.C., Police Station-Rura, District- Kanpur Dehat during the pendency of trial.

3. As per the prosecution case in brief, victim lodged F.I.R. on 24.06.2024 for the alleged offence under Sections 376 and 120-B I.P.C. against the applicant Pramod Kumar and co-accused Chhote alleging inter alia on 02.06.2024 at 10.00 P.M. when she had gone to attend call of nature in the toilet situated outside of her house, accused persons, who were already ambushing there, caught her Pramod Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111855576/

sentences.text: forcibly by dragging took her to his house where the applicant tight her mouth with clothes and committed rape whereas co-accused Chhote was standing outside the house.

When she raised alarm,
her family members reached there then both the accused persons ran away.
4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that victim and applicant both are neighbors.
The applicant has been falsely implicated on account of ill will.

The victim in her statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has changed the prosecution version improving the prosecution case stating inter alia that the applicant took her to roof of his house so that she may able to go her house whereas as per cite plan prepared by the Investigating Officer house of the victim is not situated adjacent to the house of the applicant and it is situated across the road.
Therefore, there is no occasion for the victim to go her house from the roof of house of the applicant.
It is also pointed out that the victim has denied internal examination.
Even during investigation she has not disclosed name of other family members who came on the spot on raising alarm of the victim.
The I.O. except the statement of her husband did not record the statement of any other person who had seen the incident.
It is further submitted that there is no corroborative material with regard to allegation levelled by the victim against the applicant.
Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

The applicant is languishing in jail since 21.08.2024 having no criminal history to his credit and in case he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the early disposal of the case.

5. Per contra, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that innocence of the applicant cannot be adjudged at pre-trial stage but does not dispute the above factual aspect of the matter as argued on behalf of the applicant.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that the victim has made improvement in the prosecution version in her statement recorded during investigation.
The fact disclosed by the victim in her statement is not corroborated from the cite plan.
The victim has refused her internal examination.
Therefore, possibility of false implication of the applicant cannot be ruled out.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused and submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, I am of the view that the applicant has made out a fit case for bail.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

8. Let the applicant Pramod Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate with the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.

2 (ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned before the release of the applicant on bail.
9.
